authored.objective: sv2-syntax parses three of the four PackageBodyElement alternatives into a lossless CST. The reference grammar is being derived through the six-phase pipeline: the expression layer is done, 100 of 526 units verified, and the next body of work is the type and definition-usage layer the expression layer now reaches into.
authored.next_step:
THE EXPRESSION LAYER IS DERIVED. 100/526 units verified, no conflicts outstanding. OwnedExpression's whole closure — operators, primaries, base expressions, literals, feature chains, bodies, invocations — is verified, and ElementFilterMember with it, which is the production that sent us here: it needed OwnedExpression and nothing else.
So PackageBodyElement is complete in the GRAMMAR, all four alternatives. It is NOT complete in the Rust parser, which still implements three: ElementFilterMember has a derived rule but no parser function and no coverage marker. That is the natural next increment on the sv2-syntax side, and it is now a small one.
WHERE THE DERIVATION REACHES NEXT: only two references dangle out of the expression layer, and both land in the type layer — FunctionBodyPart needs TypeBodyElement and ResultExpressionMember, ReturnFeatureMember needs FeatureElement. Deriving those opens the definition-usage layer, which is the bulk of the remaining 426 units. It is broader than the expression layer but far more repetitive: the hard structural decisions are behind us.
FIVE SPECIFICATION DEFECTS were found in the expression clauses and recorded in deviations.json, four with a filed OMG issue verified by fetching the page:
  - MetaClassificationTestOperator-casing (KERML11-112)
  - InstatiatedTypeMember-misspelling, a missing 'n'
  - InvocationTypeMember-misnomer (KERML11-83, which quotes the technical editor saying it should have been InstantiatedTypeMember; also KERML11-113, KERML11-179)
  - PositionalArgumentList-prefix, a stray 'e.' (KERML11-111)
  - and NonFeatureChainPrimaryArgument, which is defined and referenced by nothing in either language. That one is NOT recorded as a deviation, because both sources agree and the reading that leaves it unreferenced is the one that makes `a.b.c` group as `(a.b).c`. grammar_consistency.py will report it as unreachable before freeze; that is the moment to decide.
WHEN CITING AN OMG ISSUE: verify it. check_citations.py resolves receipts and file-ID shapes, not issue IDs, so a fabricated number passes every check in this repository. An adjudication reported KERML11-112 and it turned out to be real, but it was recorded only after the page was fetched and read. Where only a title and status were read and not the issue body, the evidence note says so.
THINGS A PARSER AUTHOR NEEDS, all recorded on their units:
  - Precedence and associativity are not in the grammar and cannot be; they are data in docs/operator-precedence.toml.
  - `*` is LiteralInfinity, a BinaryOperator, and the namespace-import wildcard. Nothing lexical separates them.
  - `()` is ambiguous between NullExpression and an empty ArgumentList.
  - RealValue takes `.5` and rejects `5.`.
  - Laziness is in the grammar, not the semantics: ArgumentExpression wraps its value in a reference where Argument does not, and BodyExpression is a FeatureReferenceExpression. That is what makes short-circuiting and select/collect bodies work.
  - A FeatureChain has at least two segments by construction, which is what keeps FeatureChainMember's two alternatives from overlapping.
NEXT, in order:
  1. Implement ElementFilterMember in sv2-syntax: parser function, coverage marker, rejection cases. It completes PackageBodyElement at 4/4 and needs an expression parser, so scope that first — the derived grammar now says exactly what one has to accept.
  2. Or continue phase 3 into the type layer, starting with TypeBodyElement, ResultExpressionMember and FeatureElement, which are the only two dangling references left.
  3. Phase 5 still needs RootNamespace derived before reachability or the oracle can run at all.
KNOWN GAPS in what exists:
  - Units carry 2 MB of corpus file paths in inputs.corpus_refs; recomputable and worth trimming if repository size starts to matter.
  - Trivia attachment is positional, not owned, and the convention is undecided.
  - parse_for_editor() does not exist; `sv2 parse` has no stdout product.
  - cargo-insta is not installed; a snapshot move needs manual promotion of each .snap.new with its reason.
  - Deriving needs the clause export: run .claude/scripts/export_wiki_clauses.py and set SV2_WIKI_CLAUSES, or grammar_next.py emits a pack with an empty clause and says so in spec_clause_problem.

RESOLVED as far as it can be on one machine. The wikis are pinned by receipt: 1651 atoms in .claude/state/wiki-receipts.json, each with its clause, page, the wiki's region_sha256 to the source PDF span, and a file hash. Drift now fails the gate, and a citation naming a receipt that was never pinned now fails scripts/check_citations.py. NOT resolved: the wikis are not in the repository, because their 1651 atoms carry ~2.3 MB of verbatim OMG specification prose with no licence notice, and this repository is MIT and public. So a fresh clone can verify nothing until it builds its own wikis from the specification PDFs, which are not redistributable either. Revisit only if OMG's licensing changes, or if the wiki builder can be pinned and rerun from locally-held PDFs as part of a bootstrap.

pending_decisions.question: RESOLVED. regen_state.py recorded `git log --oneline -8` in the generated block and --check compared it, which has no fixed point: the commit carrying state.json cannot record its own hash, and amending only moves it. The gate was therefore red after every commit, for ever. Fixed by naming the compared measurements explicitly — COMPARED = (coverage, tests, pins) — and a pure is_stale() over them, with four tests including the one that says a new commit is not staleness. `commits` is still measured and written for whoever reads the block at session start; it is simply not evidence. Nothing else read it: not state_report.py, not the schema's required list. NOT weakened: coverage, tests and pins are still compared exactly as before, so an un-regenerated block after real work still fails.

RESOLVED: the derive-grammar six-phase pipeline. It runs, and the expression layer is being derived through it starting from KerML 8.2.5.8.1. Two pipeline defects had to be fixed first (plan enumerated the Xtext inventory; freeze check went red on the first derived unit); both are fixed and tested.

RESOLVED. A unit no longer embeds its clause: it keeps the citation and a sha256 of the clause text, and grammar_next.py joins the text from the local export at read time. The units are therefore committed, so the derived rules, decisions and evidence survive a clone and are reviewable in a diff, while no specification prose enters the repository. check_derivation_text.py holds the line on every gate. NOT resolved by this: a fresh clone still cannot re-derive or verify a clause without building the wikis from locally-held PDFs, which is the standing wiki-reproducibility limit.
